question_html: How is depreciation defined under Schedule II to the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: The physical deterioration of an asset due to continuous usage
options.B: The systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life
options.C: The setting aside of funds for the replacement of obsolete fixed assets
options.D: The reduction in the market value of property, plant and equipment

answer_html: Answer: (B) As per Schedule II under the Companies Act, 2013, depreciation is defined as the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life[cite: 15].

question_html: When does the depreciation of an asset begin?

options.A: When the asset is purchased and paid for in full
options.B: When the asset is first physically used in production
options.C: When it is available for use, i.e., in the location and condition necessary for it to be capable of operating as intended
options.D: At the beginning of the financial year following its acquisition

answer_html: Answer: (C) Depreciation of an asset begins when it is available for use, i.e., when it is in the location and condition necessary for it to be capable of operating in the manner intended by management[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following is an essential condition for identifying a part of Property, Plant & Equipment as a separate component for component depreciation?

options.A: It must have a physical lifespan of more than 5 years
options.B: It must have both a significant cost compared to the overall item and a different useful life or depreciation method
options.C: It must be an imported part purchased separately
options.D: Its cost must be less than 10% of the total asset cost

answer_html: Answer: (B) A part of Property, Plant & Equipment to be identified as a separate component must have both significant cost compared to the overall item and an estimated useful life or depreciation method different from the rest of the parts[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following expenses should NOT be included in the cost of Property, Plant and Equipment?

options.B: Site preparation costs
options.C: Cost of staff training for conducting business in a new location
options.D: Installation and assembly costs

answer_html: Answer: (C) Cost of conducting business in a new location or with a new class of customer, including staff training costs, should not become part of the cost of the asset[cite: 15].
topic_text: Cost of Property Plant and Equipment

question_html: What is the nature of depreciation expense in financial accounting?

options.A: It is a cash outflow expense that creates an immediate reserve fund
options.B: It is a non-cash expense that does not result in any cash outflow
options.C: It is an appropriation of profit rather than a charge against profit
options.D: It is an optional expense recognized only when there is a net profit

answer_html: Answer: (B) Depreciation is a non-cash expense and unlike other normal expenditures does not result in any cash outflow[cite: 15].

question_html: Which method of depreciation results in a constant charge over the useful life of an asset if the residual value does not change?

options.B: Straight-line Method
options.C: Sum of Years of Digits Method
options.D: Depletion Method

answer_html: Answer: (B) Straight-line method results in a constant charge over the useful life if the residual value of the asset does not change[cite: 15].

question_html: Under Income Tax Rules in India, which method of depreciation is generally prescribed for assets (except for undertakings engaged in power generation and distribution)?

options.B: Diminishing Balance Method
options.C: Sum of Years of Digits Method
options.D: Production Units Method

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Income Tax Rules prescribe the Diminishing Balance Method except in the case of assets of an undertaking engaged in generation and distribution of power[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the allocation of the cost of wasting natural resources such as oil, gas, timber, and minerals to the production process called?

options.B: Depletion
options.C: Obsolescence
options.D: Flotation

answer_html: Answer: (B) Depletion is the allocation of the cost of wasting natural resources such as oil, gas, timber, and minerals to the production process[cite: 15].

question_html: When an enterprise changes its method of depreciation, how is such change treated under Accounting Standards?

options.A: As a fundamental error correction requiring retrospective adjustment
options.B: As a change in accounting estimate whose effect is quantified and disclosed separately
options.C: As an ordinary operational adjustment ignored in financial statements
options.D: As an extraordinary item transferred directly to capital reserve

answer_html: Answer: (B) Whenever any change in depreciation method is made, such change in method is treated as a change in accounting estimate as per Accounting Standards, and its effect needs to be quantified and disclosed separately[cite: 15].
topic_text: Change in the Method of Depreciation

question_html: What is the presumed maximum useful life of an intangible asset under accounting standards unless evidence exists to the contrary?

options.B: 10 years
options.C: 20 years
options.D: Indefinite

answer_html: Answer: (B) It is presumed that the useful life of an intangible asset will not exceed ten years from the date when the asset is available for use unless evidence exists to the contrary[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the residual value of an intangible asset generally assumed to be unless specific conditions are met?

options.B: Equal to original cost
options.C: Zero
options.D: Fair market value at acquisition

answer_html: Answer: (C) Given the nature of intangible assets, the residual value of an intangible asset should be assumed to be zero unless there is a commitment by a third party to purchase it or an active market exists[cite: 15].

question_html: In the case of an upward revaluation of an item of Property, Plant and Equipment, where should the increase in carrying amount be credited initially (assuming no previous decrease was debited to P&L)?

options.B: Revaluation Surplus under equity / owners' interests
options.C: General Reserve
options.D: Capital Redemption Reserve

answer_html: Answer: (B) In case the carrying amount of an asset increases due to revaluation, such increase should be credited to revaluation surplus and accumulated in equity[cite: 15].
topic_text: Revaluation of Property Plant and Equipment

question_html: What is the term used for writing off the value of intangible assets on an annual basis?

options.B: Amortisation
options.C: Depletion
options.D: Extinguishment

answer_html: Answer: (B) Intangible assets are amortised over their useful life; writing off the value of intangible assets on an annual basis is known as amortisation[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a primary objective of providing depreciation?

options.A: To ascertain true results of operations (correct income measurement)
options.B: To present true and fair view of the financial position
options.C: To create secret reserves in the business
options.D: To ascertain true cost of production

answer_html: Answer: (C) Creating secret reserves is not an objective of depreciation; the primary objectives are proper income measurement, financial position presentation, fund accumulation for replacement, and true cost ascertainment[cite: 15].

question_html: When a Provision for Depreciation Account is maintained, how is the asset account presented in the balance sheet?

options.B: At its original historical cost, while accumulated depreciation is shown separately
options.C: At its estimated replacement cost
options.D: At zero until the asset is fully disposed of

answer_html: Answer: (B) Maintaining a provision for depreciation account allows the assets to be carried at historical cost, presenting both gross investment and accumulated depreciation[cite: 15].
topic_text: Accounting Entries and Provision for Depreciation

question_html: Original cost of a machine is ₹12,60,000, salvage value is Nil, and useful life is 6 years. What is the depreciation for the first year under the sum of years digits (SYD) method?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Sum of digits = $6 \times 7 / 2 = 21$. First year depreciation = $(12,60,000 - 0) \times (6 / 21) = \text{₹}3,60,000$[cite: 15].
topic_text: Sum of Years of Digits Method Calculation

question_html: The cost of a machine is ₹20,00,000. Two years later the book value is ₹10,00,000 under straight-line method. What is the straight-line percentage depreciation?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Total depreciation in 2 years = $20,000,000 - 10,000,000 = \text{₹}10,000,000$. Annual depreciation = $5,000,000$. Rate = $(5,000,000 / 20,000,000) \times 100 = 25\%$[cite: 15].

question_html: A machinery with original cost of ₹10,00,000 and Nil salvage value acquired on 1st April 2019 with 4 years useful life was depreciated using Straight Line Method. It was sold on 1st October 2022 for ₹1,20,000. What is the gain or loss on the sale?

options.B: Gain of ₹1,20,000
options.C: Loss of ₹5,000
options.D: Gain of ₹25,000

answer_html: Answer: (C) Annual depreciation = $10,00,000 / 4 = \text{₹}2,50,000$. Depreciation for 3.5 years (up to 1 Oct 2022) = $2,50,000 \times 3.5 = \text{₹}8,75,000$. WDV = $10,00,000 - 8,75,000 = \text{₹}1,25,000$. Sale proceeds = ₹1,20,000. Loss = $1,25,000 - 1,20,000 = \text{₹}5,000$[cite: 15].
topic_text: Gain or Loss on Sale of Machine

question_html: A plant with original cost of ₹50,00,000 was revalued after 2 years resulting in a credit to Revaluation Surplus account of ₹4,00,000. Towards the year end, due to market decline, the plant value went down by ₹5,00,000. What is the impact of this downward revaluation on the Profit & Loss Account?

options.B: Debit of ₹1,00,000
options.C: Credit of ₹5,00,000
options.D: Nil impact

answer_html: Answer: (B) The downward revaluation of ₹5,00,000 first absorbs the existing Revaluation Surplus of ₹4,00,000, and the excess ₹1,00,000 is debited to the Profit & Loss Account[cite: 15].

question_html: A company developed a technology capitalized as an intangible asset at ₹5,00,000 with a 3-year estimated life. Forecasted sales percentages are 50% in year 1, 35% in year 2, and 15% in year 3. What should be the amortisation charge in the third year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Amortisation in year 3 = 15% of ₹5,00,000 = ₹75,000[cite: 15].

question_html: A machine costing ₹6,00,000 is depreciated on straight line basis assuming 10 years useful life and nil residual value for 3 years. At the end of the 3rd year, the remaining useful life was reassessed at 5 years. What is the depreciation for the 4th year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) WDV at end of 3rd year = $6,00,000 - (60,000 \times 3) = \text{₹}4,20,000$. Revised depreciation for 4th year = $4,20,000 / 5 = \text{₹}84,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: A machine costing ₹12,00,000 is depreciated straight-line assuming 10 year working life and zero residual value for 3 years. At the end of the 3rd year, the machine was revalued upwards by ₹60,000 and remaining useful life was reassessed at 9 years. What is the depreciation for the 4th year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) WDV at end of 3rd year = $12,00,000 - (1,20,000 \times 3) = \text{₹}8,40,000$. Depreciable amount after revaluation = $8,40,000 + 60,000 = \text{₹}9,00,000$. Depreciation = $9,00,000 / 9 = \text{₹}1,00,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: Prime Streaming Co. acquired streaming rights for ₹18,00,000 for 10 years. At the beginning of the 4th year, due to decline in viewership, the remaining streaming period was revised to 5 years. What is the amortisation for the 4th year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Amortisation for 3 years = $1,80,000 \times 3 = \text{₹}5,40,000$. Carrying amount at end of 3rd year = $18,00,000 - 5,40,000 = \text{₹}12,60,000$. Amortisation from 4th year = $12,60,000 / 5 = \text{₹}2,52,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: A machine was purchased for ₹30,00,000 with total estimated working hours of 24,000 and scrap value of ₹2,00,000. If effective hours worked in years 1-3 are 3,000 hours per year, what is the annual depreciation for years 1-3 under the machine hour rate method?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Depreciation per hour = $(30,00,000 - 2,00,000) / 24,000 = \text{₹}1,16.67$. Annual depreciation for years 1-3 = $(3,000 / 24,000) \times 28,00,000 = \text{₹}3,50,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: M/s Surya & Co. took a quarry lease on 1-1-2019 for ₹1,00,00,000 with an estimated mineral deposit of 2,00,000 tonnes. If the quantity extracted in 2019 was 2,000 tonnes, what is the depreciation charged for 2019 under the depletion method?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Depletion per tonne = $1,00,000,000 / 2,00,000 = \text{₹}50$. Depreciation for 2019 = $2,000 \times 50 = \text{₹}1,00,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following is considered a tangible asset holding physical substance?

options.B: Goodwill
options.C: Machinery
options.D: Trademarks

answer_html: Answer: (C) Machinery is a tangible asset having physical substance, whereas patents, goodwill, and trademarks are intangible assets[cite: 15].

question_html: What does the term 'depreciable amount' mean in relation to an asset?

options.A: The historical cost plus estimated scrap value
options.B: The historical cost or other amount substituted for cost, less its residual value
options.C: The market value of the asset at the end of its useful life
options.D: The total repairs and maintenance incurred over the asset's life

answer_html: Answer: (B) Depreciable amount is the cost of an asset or other amount substituted for cost less its residual value[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following causes of depreciation is related to efflux of time even when the asset is not being used?

options.A: Wear and tear due to use
options.B: Passage of time / efflux of time
options.C: Technological obsolescence
options.D: Depletion of minerals

answer_html: Answer: (B) Efflux of time causes a decrease in the value of assets even when they are not being physically used[cite: 15].

question_html: What accounting entry is passed to record depreciation when a Provision for Depreciation Account is maintained?

options.A: Debit Asset A/c, Credit Depreciation A/c
options.B: Debit Depreciation A/c, Credit Provision for Depreciation A/c
options.C: Debit Profit and Loss A/c, Credit Asset A/c
options.D: Debit Provision for Depreciation A/c, Credit Profit and Loss A/c

answer_html: Answer: (B) Depreciation Account is debited and Provision for Depreciation (Accumulated Depreciation) Account is credited[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following methods of depreciation results in a decreasing annual charge over the useful life of the asset?

options.B: Reducing Balance Method
options.C: Machine Hour Method with constant usage
options.D: Production Units Method with constant production

answer_html: Answer: (B) Diminishing Balance Method results in a decreasing charge over the useful life of the asset[cite: 15].

question_html: Kumar R&D Co. registered a patent on 1st July 2021 developed at a cost of ₹28,00,000 and spent ₹2,00,000 towards legal fees and registration for a 10-year period. Books are closed on 31st December. What is the amortisation for the year 2021?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total patent cost = $28,00,000 + 2,00,000 = \text{₹}30,00,000$. Annual amortisation = $30,00,000 / 10 = \text{₹}3,00,000$. For 6 months (July to Dec 2021) = $3,00,000 \times (6/12) = \text{₹}1,50,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: A machine is purchased for ₹20,00,000 with estimated useful life of 10 years and residual value of ₹2,00,000, expected to produce 1.5 lakh units. If production in years 1-3 is 20,000 units per year, what is the annual depreciation under the production units method?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Depreciable amount = $20,00,000 - 2,00,000 = \text{₹}18,00,000$. Annual depreciation = $(20,000 / 1,50,000) \times 18,00,000 = \text{₹}2,40,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: An asset costing ₹1,10,000 with residual value of ₹10,000 and 5 years useful life has depreciation calculated as per straight line method. What is the annual depreciation?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Depreciable amount = $1,10,000 - 10,000 = \text{₹}1,00,000$. Depreciation = $1,00,000 / 5 = \text{₹}20,000$ per year[cite: 15].

question_html: If the equipment account has a balance of ₹22,50,000 and the accumulated depreciation account has a balance of ₹14,00,000, what is the book value of the equipment?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Book value = Original Cost - Accumulated Depreciation = $22,50,000 - 14,00,000 = \text{₹}8,50,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: Amazing Group had PP&E with a book value of ₹35,00,000 on 31st December 2022 and Revaluation Surplus of ₹3,00,000. Revaluation on that date resulted in a fair value of ₹37,00,000. What is the resulting balance in Revaluation Surplus?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Upward revaluation = $37,00,000 - 35,00,000 = \text{₹}2,00,000$. Added to existing surplus of ₹3,00,000, total Revaluation Surplus becomes ₹5,00,000[cite: 15].

question_html: Amazing Group had PP&E with a book value of ₹35,00,000 and Revaluation Surplus of ₹3,00,000 on 31st December 2022. Revaluation on that date resulted in a fair value of ₹31,00,000. How is the decrease accounted for?

options.B: Debit Revaluation Surplus ₹3,00,000 and Debit P&L A/c ₹1,00,000
options.C: Debit P&L A/c ₹4,00,000
options.D: Debit Revaluation Surplus ₹1,00,000 and Debit P&L A/c ₹3,00,000

answer_html: Answer: (B) Downward revaluation of ₹4,00,000 first utilizes the entire Revaluation Surplus of ₹3,00,000, and the excess ₹1,00,000 is debited to the Profit & Loss Account[cite: 15].

question_html: A machinery costing ₹20,00,000 is depreciated on straight line assuming 10 years life and nil salvage value for 4 years. At the end of the 4th year, it was revalued upwards by ₹80,000 and remaining useful life was reassessed as 8 years. What is the depreciation for the 5th year?
answer_html: Answer: (B) WDV at end of 4th year = $20,00,000 - (2,00,000 \times 4) = \text{₹}12,00,000$. New depreciable amount = $12,00,000 + 80,000 = \text{₹}12,80,000$. Depreciation for 5th year = $12,80,000 / 8 = \text{₹}1,60,000$[cite: 15].
topic_text: Depreciation after Upward Revaluation and Life Revision

question_html: Jain Bros. acquired a machine on 1st July 2021 at a cost of ₹14,00,000 and spent ₹1,00,000 on installation, closing books on 31st December. If depreciation is written off at 10% p.a. on original cost every year, what is the depreciation for 2022?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total capitalized cost = $14,00,000 + 1,00,000 = \text{₹}15,00,000$. Annual depreciation = 10% of ₹15,00,000 = ₹1,50,000[cite: 15].
topic_text: Straight Line Depreciation on Original Cost

question_html: Jain Bros. acquired a machine on 1st July 2021 at a cost of ₹14,00,000 and spent ₹1,00,000 on installation, closing books on 31st December. Under diminishing balance method at 10% p.a., what is the WDV at the end of 2022?
M/s Akash & Co. purchased a machine for ₹10,00,000 (estimated useful life 10 years, scrap value ₹1,20,000) on 1.1.2017. What is the depreciation for 2022 using the sum of years digits method?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Depreciable amount = $10,00,000 - 1,20,000 = \text{₹}8,80,000$. For 2022 (6th year of life), remaining life including current year is 5 years. SYD depreciation = $8,80,000 \times (5 / 55) = \text{₹}80,000$[cite: 15].
topic_text: Sum of Years Digits Method Advanced Calculation

question_html: What is the primary feature of the Straight Line Method of depreciation?

options.A: Depreciation decreases every year based on diminishing balance
options.B: An equal amount of depreciation is written off every year
options.C: Depreciation is calculated solely based on units produced
options.D: Depreciation is charged only in years when the asset makes a profit

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under the straight-line method, an equal amount is written off every year during the working life of an asset[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following intangible asset examples represents broadcasting or streaming permissions?

options.B: Trademarks
options.C: Streaming rights on platforms like Netflix or Disney+ Hotstar
options.D: Purchased goodwill

answer_html: Answer: (C) Streaming rights of movies/shows on platforms like Netflix or Amazon Prime are classic examples of intangible assets[cite: 15].

question_html: What does 'Control' mean in the context of recognizing intangible assets?

options.A: The physical possession of a certificate of registration
options.B: The power available with the enterprise to obtain economic benefits from the asset and restrict access of others
options.C: The absolute legal ownership granted by the government without time limits
options.D: The ability to trade the asset in an open market without restrictions

answer_html: Answer: (B) Control means the power available with the enterprise to obtain economic benefits from the asset and restrict access of others to those benefits[cite: 15].

question_html: How should gains or losses arising from the retirement or disposal of an intangible asset be recognized?

options.B: Recognized as income or expense in the statement of profit and loss
options.C: Adjusted against opening retained earnings without P&L routing
options.D: Capitalized as part of goodwill

answer_html: Answer: (B) Gains or losses from retirement or disposal of an intangible asset are recognized as income or expense in the statement of profit and loss[cite: 15].

question_html: What is an alternative account that can be opened in the ledger to calculate profit or loss on the sale of a tangible asset instead of posting directly in the asset account?

options.B: Realisation Account
options.C: Suspense Account
options.D: Depreciation Adjustment Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) An Asset Disposal Account may be opened in the ledger to calculate profit or loss on the sale of an asset[cite: 15].

question_html: A firm purchased a machine on 1st January 2020 for ₹5,82,000 and spent ₹18,000 on erection. On 1st July 2020, another machine for ₹2,00,000 was acquired. Depreciation is 10% p.a. on WDV. On 1st July 2021, the first machine was auctioned for ₹3,86,000. What is the loss on sale of the first machine?
topic_text: Loss on Sale under WDV Method

question_html: On 1st April 2019, LG Transport Co. purchased 10 trucks at ₹45,00,000 each. On 1st October 2021, one truck was destroyed in an accident and ₹27,00,000 was received from insurance in full settlement. Depreciation is 20% p.a. on original cost (calendar year financial year). What is the profit or loss on settlement of the truck?

options.B: Profit of ₹4,50,000
options.C: Loss of ₹4,50,000
options.D: Nil profit or loss

answer_html: Answer: (B) WDV of one truck at 1.1.2021 = ₹29,25,000. Dep for 9 months in 2021 = ₹6,75,000. WDV at date of accident = ₹22,50,000. Insurance recovery = ₹27,00,000. Profit = $27,00,000 - 22,50,000 = \text{₹}4,50,000$[cite: 15].

question_html: What should happen to Revaluation Surplus when a revalued asset is derecognized (retired or disposed of)?

options.A: Transferred through P&L statement as part of operating income
options.B: Transferred directly to retained earnings / reserves without routing through P&L
options.C: Written off against share capital
options.D: Permanently retained in revaluation surplus account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revaluation surplus may be transferred directly to retained earnings when the asset is derecognized, and cannot be made through the Profit or Loss[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the key difference between tangible and intangible assets regarding useful life presumptions?

options.A: Tangible assets have a presumed 10-year limit, while intangible assets have no limits
options.B: Tangible assets have useful life based on expected usage with no presumption laid down, whereas intangible assets have a presumption not to exceed 10 years
options.C: Intangible assets are never presumed to have a finite life
options.D: There is no difference in their useful life presumptions

answer_html: Answer: (B) Tangible assets have a useful life based on expected usage with no presumption laid down, whereas intangible assets are presumed not to exceed 10 years unless evidence exists to the contrary[cite: 15].
topic_text: Tangible vs Intangible Useful Life Presumption

question_html: Why is it necessary to charge depreciation as an item of cost of production?

options.A: To reduce tax liabilities to zero
options.B: To ascertain the true cost of production and match expired asset cost against revenues generated
options.C: To inflate asset values on the balance sheet
options.D: To avoid maintaining an asset register

answer_html: Answer: (B) Charging depreciation is necessary for proper income measurement, matching expenses with revenues, and ascertaining true cost of production[cite: 15].
